newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish opposition submits new censure motion.
newsitem.headline: Turkish opposition submits new censure motion.

text.p: Turkey's main opposition Motherland Party (ANAP) on Friday submitted a censure motion against the Islamist-led government in the latest parliamentary challenge to Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan's rule.
Anatolian news agency reported the party said the government had abused its position by giving security forces larger wage rises than other public employees in a recent round of salary increases.

Parliamentary sources said MPs would probably vote on the motion along with two other opposition challenges on February 25 in what will effectively be a confidence vote on the seven-month-old coalition government.
Two leftist parties have tabled a motion for the administration to be toppled for allegedly threatening Turkey's official secularism. The government has a majority of five in the 550-seat assembly.
It also faces votes next week on whether to send Deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller to the Supreme Court on three separate corruption charges dating back to her time as prime minister from 1993-96.
Ciller heads the True Path Party coalition partner and is also foreign minister.
